stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def fill_between_1s_fixed(g):
    """Fill cells between any pair of 1s, but preserve 1s"""
    result = [row[:] for row in g]
    
    # First, make a copy of 1 positions to know what to preserve
    ones_positions = set((r, c) for r in range(len(g)) for c in range(len(g[0])) if g[r][c] == 1)
    
    # Horizontal fill
    for r in range(len(g)):
        ones_in_row = sorted([c for c in range(len(g[r])) if g[r][c] == 1])
        for pair in list(combinations(ones_in_row, 2)):
            c1, c2 = pair
            for c in range(c1 + 1, c2):
                if (r, c) not in ones_positions:  # Don't overwrite 1s
                    result[r][c] = 3
    
    # Vertical fill
    for c in range(len(g[0])):
        ones_in_col = sorted([r for r in range(len(g)) if g[r][c] == 1])
        for pair in list(combinations(ones_in_col, 2)):
            r1, r2 = pair
            for r in range(r1 + 1, r2):
                if (r, c) not in ones_positions:  # Don't overwrite 1s

def adjacency_filter(g):
    """
    Idea: Cell becomes 3 only if 
    - NOT row-surrounded (has 1 on BOTH left AND right, i.e. 1...3...1 pattern)
    - NOT col-surrounded (has 1 on BOTH top AND bottom, i.e. 1...3...1 vertically)
    
    Cells between two dots have 1 on one side and 1/dot on the other - not both 1
    """
    H, W = 28, 11
    result = [[int(x) for x in row] for row in g]
    dot = 7
    
    # Mark which cells have 1 on both left and right
    row_surrounded = [[False] * W for _ in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(1, W - 1):
            if result[r][c - 1] == 1 and result[r][c + 1] == 1:
                row_surrounded[r][c] = True
    
    # Mark which cells have 1 on both top and bottom
    col_surrounded = [[False] * W for _ in range(H)]
    for c in range(W):
        for r in range(1, H - 1):
            if result[r - 1][c] == 1 and result[r + 1][c] == 1:
                col_surrounded[r][c] = True
    
    # A fill candidate is: between two dots in row OR between two dots in col
    # Don't apply if already surrounded (would become 1-1-3-1-1)
    
    # First mark all cells between dots
    fill_candidates = [[False] * W for _ in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        dots = [c for c in range(W) if g[r][c] == dot]
        for i in range(len(dots) - 1):
            for c in range(dots[i] + 1, dots[i + 1]):
                fill_candidates[r][c] = True
        for i in range(len(dots) - 1):
            for c in range(dots[i] + 1, dots[i + 1]):
                fill_candidates[r][c] = True
    
    for c in range(W):
        dots = [r for r in range(H) if g[r][c] == dot]
        for i in range(len(dots) - 1):
            for r in range(dots[i] + 1, dots[i + 1]):
                fill_candidates[r][c] = True
    
    # Now apply fill logic
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if fill_candidates[r][c] and result[r][c] == 1:
                # Don't fill if surrounded (1...1...1)
                if not row_surrounded[r][c] and not col_surrounded[r][c]:
                    result[r][c] = 3
    
    cnt = Counter(val for r in result for val in r)
    print(f"Adjacency filter: {cnt}")
    
    # Print fill locations
    fills = [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if result[r][c] == 3]
    print(f"Total fills: {len(fills)}")
